articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Kenshi Unofficial Multiplayer Mod The Kenshi Unofficial Multiplayer Mod is a community‑developed project that enables limited cooperative multiplayer functionality in Kenshi, the single‑player squad‑based sandbox RPG created by Lo‑Fi Games. While Kenshi was designed and released as a strictly offline, single‑player experience, this mod attempts to synchronize core gameplay systems across multiple clients, allowing players to explore, build, and fight together within a shared world. The project is not affiliated with Lo‑Fi Games and is considered experimental, with varying levels of stability depending on version, host hardware, and player count. You can self-host this mod or rent from a dedicated game server provider. Overview The mod introduces a lightweight client–server architecture that allows one player to host a world while others connect as clients. It focuses on synchronizing essential gameplay elements such as character movement, combat states, inventory changes, and world events. Due to the complexity of Kenshi’s simulation engine, the mod does not provide full parity with single‑player behavior, but it enables a functional cooperative experience for small groups. The mod is primarily aimed at players who want to share exploration, base building, and squad management with friends while accepting the limitations of unofficial multiplayer support. Features Multiplayer Connectivity Host‑client model with LAN or internet connections Support for 2–6 players depending on system performance Optional password‑protected sessions Character & Squad Synchronization Real‑time syncing of player‑controlled characters Shared or separate squads depending on host settings Basic AI behavior replicated across clients Combat Synchronization Position, animation, and health state syncing Shared aggro and enemy targeting Occasional desync may occur during large battles World & Base Building Shared access to buildings, crafting stations, and storage Construction progress synchronized across clients Research tree shared between all players Inventory & Economy Trading between players Shared access to shops and vendors Item pickup, crafting output, and container contents synced Limitations Because Kenshi was not designed for multiplayer, several systems remain partially implemented or unstable: Pathfinding desync during large squad movements Occasional rubber‑banding in crowded cities AI schedules not always consistent across clients Weather and lighting may visually differ between players Save files are host‑only and not cross‑compatible with vanilla saves Mods that alter AI, factions, or world states may cause conflicts The developers of the mod recommend small group play and avoiding extremely large squads to maintain stability. Installation The mod is typically distributed through Nexus Mods or GitHub. Installation generally involves: Downloading the mod package Extracting it into the Kenshi mods directory Enabling the mod in the game launcher Running the included multiplayer launcher or executable Configuring host settings and sharing the session IP with friends Some versions include a dedicated server tool, while others rely on the host running both the game and the server instance simultaneously. Development The Kenshi Unofficial Multiplayer Mod is maintained by independent modders and reverse‑engineering enthusiasts. Development focuses on: Improving synchronization stability Expanding support for AI‑heavy scenarios Reducing crashes during large battles Enhancing compatibility with popular overhaul mods Because the mod relies on memory hooks and engine‑level workarounds, updates to Kenshi may temporarily break compatibility until the mod is patched. Community Reception The mod has been praised for making cooperative Kenshi gameplay possible for the first time, especially for exploration‑focused groups. Players enjoy the ability to: Build bases together Run squads in parallel Explore dangerous regions as a team However, the mod is also known for instability, occasional crashes, and desync issues. Most players view it as a “fun experiment” rather than a fully polished multiplayer mode. References Kenshi Github Page[1]

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: WIP This information is from Boron & Lucius. The item given is conjured from nothing, does not need to be in the NPC’s possession. How to give maps, weapons or armor via dialogue This is based on the fact, that through dialogue an object is given using its StringID. The game only checks if an item is ‘givable’ when the modder adds the item on the dialogue using the give item drop down. The list is populated by object type, defined in the fcs.def file (in Kenshi installation folder). Although the fcs.def allows only one object type listed there, one can change that any time as long as they restart the FCS each time they want to change object types. Thus, it is possible for one single NPC, in one dialogue give multiple different types of objects. Each item just has to be set on a different dialogue line. And one must take care to not accidentally change the item once the fcs.def is changed for a different type (or you would have to do the change again). Set up your NPC and their dialogue normally. Set a separate line of dialogue for each item. When you are ready to add the item, open its file and see what object type it is. Save and close fcs entirely. Click open fcs.def (you need either Visual Studio Community or Notepad++) Edit line 875; give item (in yellow below) Replace the word ITEM (in blue below) with the object type you want, all caps with underlines if any. Do not change the boolean (1). Save the fcs.def and open FCS again. Add the desired object to the dialogue line normally using the give item feature. The drop down menu is now populated with your chosen object type. Repeat steps 5 to 7 for each item type you want to give to the player. It may be this NPC only gives armor, if then you do not need another change. Do not forget to change the fcs.def line 875 back to ITEM after you finish. Weapons Weapons are a bit trickier, as they are divided into Manufacturer groups. Meaning you can only put the WEAPON_MANUFACTURER on the fcs.def file, and doing so your give item list will only be populated with weapon manufacturers. But that is the ONLY WAY to get textured weapons, because the texture is attached to the manufacturer of the weapon. So if you put WEAPON on the line 875, you would get the mesh reference, and not a weapon with stats and a texture. It will also crash the game. HOWEVER this means you cannot pick one special weapon to be given UNLESS you make a special manufacturer with only that one weapon in the list. What Object Types are compatible? Any item that can be put inside the player inventory. I would assume buildables will probably crash the game. If you find it under the Item category in FCS, it should work, excluding naturally the material files and such sub files. Containers below refer to bags. ITEM, MAP_ITEM, ARMOR, CONTAINER, WEAPON_MANUFACTURER, CROSSBOW, NEST_ITEM, CHARACTER_PHYSICS_ATTACHMENT, LIMB_REPLACEMENT And YES the same trick also applies to target has item on the line 886. But the item may not be equipped when the NPC does the testing. Note we have not tested all these, so please comment below if you crash or something. Rumor has it one can also give RESEARCH. These works also as special items, but alas RESEARCH crashes the game as special items. Speaking of, yes this method works as both research cost and material cost in machines. In theory, I did not test if they make the game crash. Lucius also has this info https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/2909495250/3887227031502321150/ “[Note that changing item type like this, given] crossbows and prosthetic limbs are level 0 and are displayed as prototype grade. Armor is also level 0, but is treated as level 100, so it will have a performance level higher than the masterwork level 95. (The grade is not displayed, but the price and weight follow the inventory settings.)“ See also A Workaround How to Make Weapons Lootable by NPCs List of FCS.def file lines where you can use this workaround Always remember to change it back after, so you do not forget you changed it later when you wonder why you do not get items for your inventory. articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: This article is a Work in Progress. It may contain out of date or incomplete information. This information is from Boron and Lucius. You can make weapons lootable by bandits by making Kenshi think the sword is bread. “It’s dumb and should probably only be used for some random junk swords.” You can edit the fcs.def file with Visual Studio Community or Notepad++. Add missing info to the base item category (ie where bread and bandages etc are) for weapons (eg sheath data, combat data) Add a weapon but make it ITEM itemtype Set the item function to FOOD_RESTRICTED. Now the sword is inedible bread Replace an NPC or Vendor’s weapon reference with the bread sword For some reason when a sword is generated, the weapon manufacturer yeets a bunch of the information (like the “possibly edible” tag) and replaces it with weapon info. So now you’ve got an actual sword that Bandits think is a food item, and they’ll steal it Boron: “You need the sword to be the base ITEM type, with function set to FOOD_RESTRICTED. You then need to copy a bunch of info from the [WEAPON] entry in fcs.def to the ITEM entry (can’t remember exactly what you need off hand), and make a new item entry, adding the data (eg sheath mesh, bare sword mesh, etc) to your item. Then that item needs to be added to an NPC as a weapon by changing weapon: WEAPON to weapon: ITEM Type of thing idk if I’ll even use—if Ido it’ll be for some of the low level swords only because it’s not like a bandit looting it will trigger the stealing weapon dialogue. Don’t want the player to miss the fact that the bandit is taking their expensive sword, that’s lame. This only works with weapons, not armour. Or rather, it might work with armour, but you still have things like [Possibly edible] in the armour description; for some reason the weapon manufacturer data overrides a bunch of information in the UI tooltip” See also A Workaround How To Give Maps, Armor or Weapons Through Dialogue

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: What is a texture map A map is a 2D representation of the garment topography. Easiest to understand by thinking about the UV map. UV map being the key, determining all the other maps for the same garment. Traditionally a 3D object (our garment) can have multiple maps; diffuse, normal, roughness, metalness, ambient occlusion, mask. Kenshi uses only three for a garment; the color map (a mask), the normal map and the diffuse aka texture map. Kenshi CAN use a roughness map, but it must be set as an alpha mask on the diffuse map. Diffuse map aka the texture Diffuse is the main texture of the garment. It contains the colors of the garment (or neutral base one can paint color on with a color map). This is where most manual effort is usually put. Defining shininess/roughness on the diffuse map Kenshi takes its cue how shiny an item is from the alpha channel of the diffuse map. If you have no alpha at all, Kenshi interprets it fully shiny and you see dark shiny film over your garment in game. There are following methods you can use to mitigate the shiny: Newb: ignore it altogether and just turn the specular value to zero in FCS. The result is 100% matte and a bit boring. Beginner: turn the entire thing 100% transparent (select all, hit del). Same result as 1. Median: use the selection tool to make separate areas for different transparency values, creating better suited shininess for parts of the garment that are shiny, like metal, and parts that are not that shiny like fabric and the eraser tool to ‘delete’ with corresponding % value. This is perfectly acceptable as an end result for a mod. Advanced: using the eraser tool to paint variations of transparency on the alpha channel, can be a pro-option if you are very good. Pro: using a roughness map as an alpha mask 1: How to turn specular off Open FCS and the item file of the garment and the material file of the garment. Go to specular field Turn the value to 0 2: How to turn the diffuse map/texture 100% alpha in Gimp You need an image editing software, preferably something that can export in .dds format with mipmaps. We recommend Gimp, it is free and deals natively with the same values as Kenshi does, so you do not have to adjust your workspace settings. Open the image of the texture in Gimp. It can be of .png, .jpg or many other formats. Go to Layer - Transparency - Add alpha channel Ctrl + A selects everything Hit the delete button. This will turn the entire image 100% transparent (not shiny). Export as .dds (replace png with dds), DXT5 compression and mipmaps enabled 3: How to use the selection and eraser tools to make different parts of the image to have different alpha values Open the image of the texture in Gimp. It can be of .png, .jpg or many other formats. Go to Layer - Transparency - Add alpha channel Pick the selection tool, any of them and select one area to be edited If you are using the loop selection tool, finalize selecting with enter. Pick the eraser tool and change the opacity value to what you want for this area (0 == totally shiny, 100 == totally matte). Adjust the hardness to 100% Change the size of the eraser tool to cover the entire texture Click ONCE on the image. Do this to all the different areas you want different transparency values on. Export as .dds (replace png with dds), DXT5 compression and mipmaps enabled 4: How to use the eraser tool to paint variation on the alpha layer You can also use the eraser tool as a paint brush to make things less shiny. You just have to use your artistic skill to determine which parts you want less shiny and which parts can remain fully (or whatever your starting value is) shiny. Generally, edges are shinier on metal objects and undersides are not shiny at all or barely shiny. This method is not really used that often, because most software used to generate textures automatically can generate a roughness map. But if you for some reason need to, you know you can manually draw with the eraser tool. 5: How to use a roughness map in Gimp for Kenshi Now if you are a machine texture generator user, like fe. substance painter, you get your hands on an automatically generated roughness map. Naturally one can make such manually as well, if one knows their way around the paint brushes etc. and knows the UV map of the garment, which part is which. For Kenshi the roughness is set in the alpha channel of the diffuse map. Basically, you use the roughness as an alpha mask. Black = 100% alpha (full matte) White = 0% alpha (fully shiny). You might have to invert your roughness map if it is generated the opposite way. Roughness/mask image: Select the image you want to use as the mask and copy it to the clipboard (ctrl + A, ctrl + C). Open the target texture image in Gimp. It can be of .png, .jpg or many other formats. Go to Layer - Transparency - Add alpha channel In the Layers selection, right-click on the layer you want to mask and select Add Layer Mask (you should have only one layer). In the ‘Add a Mask to the Layer’ menu, choose an initialization option, such as ‘White (full opacity)’, and click Add. Click on the mask thumbnail in the Layers dialog to make it the active editing element. With the layer mask active, paste the image from the clipboard onto the mask. Right-click the floating selection in the Layers dialog and select Anchor Layer or click the anchor icon in the Layers dialog to merge it with the layer mask. Export as .dds (replace png with dds), DXT5 compression and mipmaps enabled Normal map Normal map is the purplish-blue texture. Normal map acts like the bump map of old, it generates lighting and shadow values on the texture as if the 3D model had more details on its geometry. It fakes 3D details, saving computational burden from the physics engine. It does not have to calculate how this 3D text on the garment behaves. The colors in general are: purple = up and teal = down, pink = right and blue = left. But Kenshi is somewhat ambiguous with these and can independently decide which is which, if the geometry of the garment is easy to interpret. Purple and Teal values are usually the only ones you need to manually change, if any. Normal map usage is very straight forward: you export it as .dds, mipmaps enabled and set the link on the garment’s material file to point to it in the mod folders. Transparency on a normal map In Kenshi a garment can have some parts transparent on it, like a crack on an armor or a hole on a shirt. This can be achieved by cutting those bits away on the normal map in image editing software and setting the material to ALPHA. Kenshi however supports only full transparency on a normal map, so no fuzzy edges, sorry. The only exception to this is the shirt layer, where the vest normal map can have partial transparency. Color Map In depth how to for beginners is available here: How to make a color map for your armor Blue channel on the color map is reserved for metallic. So, if you have a metalness map from texture map generating software (like substance painter), you can just use the metalness map as a mask on the blue color channel of the color map.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: This page is a direct translation from Japanese of this page: https://wiki3.jp/kenshijp/page/612 Credit & images: Momayo Preparing the necessary software Installing RE_Kenshi Download and install RE_Kenshi from this page: https://www.nexusmods.com/kenshi/mods/847 Check out the sound modification method published on the RE_Kenshi Wiki on this page. For the basics of sound modification, please refer to https://github.com/BFrizzleFoShizzle/RE_Kenshi/wiki/Using-RE_Kenshi-to-mod-sound-banks Installing Wwise version 2014.1.3 You can download and install it from this page https://wiki.totalwar.com/w/Wwise_-_Audio_Moding. Please be sure to check the license terms before downloading. The package available for download from this page is distributed for the game Total War: ROME II. It seems that any version of Wise prior to 2015.1.9 should be fine (unconfirmed). Currently (July 2023), the oldest version of Wwise officially available from Audiokinetic is 2016.1.6, but Kenshi was unable to load the version using this. After installing Wwise 2014.1.3, if you receive the error “The application could not be started due to an incorrect side-by-side configuration” upon launch, please install Microsoft Visual C++ 2008. You will also need a sound editing software. Format The audio files used for sound editing are in .wav format with a sampling frequency of 44100hz. Use these software programs to edit and convert audio files: Audacity https://www.audacityteam.org/ Sound Engine (link removed) Windows version (link removed) [Cattrina: these links seem to no longer work] Get the sound event name Basically, you can edit the sound by following the instructions in the RE_Kenshi WIKI above. However, this alone will not tell you the necessary Kenshi sound event name, so you will need to get it. After installing RE_Kenshi, start the game. The RE_Kenshi Menu will appear, so check [Log audio IDs/events/switches/states]. If the RE_Kenshi Menu does not appear or if you have closed the window, you can make it appear again by going to [Options] → [MOD] → [RE_Kenshi settings]. When [Log audio IDs/events/switches/states] is checked, the sound event name will be output to the Debug log tab of RE_Kenshi Menu the first time a sound is played in the game. You can see that the sound event name for the sound made when you hover the mouse cursor over each button on the title screen is “Hover,” the sound made when you click is “General_Click,” and the “jaggiiiiiiing” sound made when a starting new game or loading is “Create_or_Load_Game.” This is the string after event: in the log. While looking at the Debug log tab, proceed until the desired sound is played in the game, and identify the sound event name. Sounds that can be triggered at any time, such as stealth, are not played automatically by NPCs and are easy to identify. Once you have obtained the sound event name, you can proceed as described on the RE_Kenshi Wiki. The RE_Kenshi debug log is output to RE_Kenshi_log.txt in the Kenshi installation folder. This log is overwritten every time the game is started, so be sure to save the log separately once you have obtained a good sound event name. Setting up FCS and adding sound events It has been discovered that it is possible to edit and add sounds to specific animations by editing the FCS Animation Event item. The object types to which Animation Event items can be added are ANIMATION, ANIMAL_ANIMATION, and COMBAT_TECHNIQUE (there may be others as well). As an example, we will edit the sound of the two-stage slash in the vanilla sword animation and add separate sounds for the first and second strikes. In preparation, we used voice synthesis software to prepare audio files for the lines “Nidan!” and “Giri!” Create a new Animation Event item and set a unique name for the Audio event. The name you set here will also be used in Wwise. Make sure it does not overlap with other event names of the Combat Techniques items, Downward combo is the two-stage animation we will be editing this time. Delete Attack and Attack 2 from the events on the right and set the two Animation Events you created earlier instead. The number to the right of the item name is likely the frame number on which the sound event will occur. Enter the numbers for Attack and Attack 2 that you deleted. Open Wwise and create an event with the same name as the event you entered. The rest of the process is the same as in the RE_Kenshi Wiki. In this successful example, during the two-stage sword slash motion, we were able to have the synthesized voice say “Nidan!” For the first strike and “Giri!” For the second strike. Sounds like this can be added to almost any animation, not just weapons motions, but also when using furniture or during standby motions. The sounds you add are not limited to lines, and you can add a variety of sounds depending on your ideas. Please be sure to check the terms and conditions when using sound materials. If you want to add sound to an existing animation, if the total number of frames in that animation is 1 (still animation), the sound will continue to play every frame, which won’t work. In that case, you can solve the problem by editing the animation using Blender and increasing the number of frames. You may also be able to adjust the frequency at which the sound reaches the frame of the animation where it will be played by adjusting the play speed in the FCS settings. Sound volume attenuation setting based on camera distance If you don’t do this, the custom sound will sound quite loud. Select the sound you want to set from the Audio tab and open the Positioning tab of the Sound Property Editor. Select 3D, select New… from Attenuation [>>], give it a name, and select Edit… to open the Attenuation Editor. (It seems that the Mode and Position Source can be configured to do more advanced things, but this has not been investigated yet. Please do as shown in the image.) The Attenuation Editor allows you to set the distance and intensity curve for each property. Generally, it sounds good to leave the default Output Bus volume as a straight line sloping downward to the right. You can also change the maximum distance (length of the horizontal axis) in the Max distance box at the bottom right. Right-click on the curve to change the curve type and double-click to add a point. Of the properties on the bottom left, setting the low-pass filter will naturally muffle the sound as the camera moves farther away from the sound source. This tends to give a better effect than just using the Output Bus volume. The low-pass filter curve rises to the right because it indicates how well it affects the camera as the distance increases. To easily check how the low-pass filter will sound, return to the Sound Property Editor and increase the Low-pass filter appropriately in the General Settings tab. Switch Configuration Some sound events are set to change the sound that is played depending on the conditions when the sound occurs. This setting is called a switch. The voice that is played when a humanoid character is hit is the event name “VO_Get_Hit”, but the sound that is played is determined by the switch group “VO_Races” for the race and gender of the character that was hit. A fairly rough conceptual diagram If you see Switch: XXX YYY in the RE_Kenshi log, XXX is the switch group name, and the YYY next to it, separated by a space, is the switch name. Event: ZZZ and Switch: XXX YYY can be output in different places in the log, so it can be a bit difficult to figure out which event has which switch. Please note that sound editing using RE_Kenshi and Wwise involves overwriting and adding on an event-by-event basis. For an event where a switch is set, all sounds within that switch group must be set. For example, if you create an event that replaces only the sound for the Hive in the switch group, the sounds for other races when hit will disappear. If you want to change only a specific part of a switch group and leave the rest as vanilla, you will need to extract the vanilla sound bank, identify the relevant sound file, and then re-set it within the switch group. Regarding extracting the vanilla sound bank, please refer to the instructions in the editing section. AI Goals AI Goals are the specific actions a character can take. They can be given to the actor via squad AI Packages, the race menu, character menu, AI contracts, or the “change AI“ dialogue effect. Classification How important is this action? Urgent Eg player orders, combat, first aid. Non-urgent Eg sleep, eating, surgery. The stuff you don’t consider on the battlefield. Fluff Ambient stuff that achieves nothing eg chatting. Just Action Obedience Max Size Ending What happens when the task is completed? Does it get removed for myself, the whole squad, or does it remain active? Nothing This is what the vast majority of goals use. Remove Mine Only As an example, this is used by the “Run away!” goal. Remove Whole Squads As an example, this is used by the “Assault on Target Squad” goal. Targeting Who to use the action on. For example, do you heal yourself or someone else? Clears Existing Jobs A boolean condition of some sort. All previous tasks end. True False Signal Function Controls how this package starts / ends. On individual item pages for Armour, one can find stats for each type and quality level of armor items. The stats listed may appear different than in game. This is because the game displays some values incorrectly. (Katanas showing as having -39% robot damage as an example) These stats, however, are determined internally by the following formulae[1]: (Important to add that items cannot have more than 90% Cut resistance or Blunt resistance. Items which would have higher than 90% (Masterwork Samurai Helmet as an example) will stop at 90% Cut resistance. Cut Resistance = (Level +/- Level Bonus) * (Class * Material+ Def Bonus) + (Material Bonus * Class) Blunt Resistance = (Level +/- Level Bonus) * (Class * Material+ Def Bonus) + (Material Bonus * Class) Harpoon Resistance = (Level +/- Level Bonus) *Material*armors multiplier Athletics, combat speed, and stealth all use the same formula to calculate their bonuses ; S t a t E f f e c t = A r m o r s M u l t i p l i e r ∗ ( ( C l a s s M a x − C l a s s M i n ) ∗ ( L e v e l ± L e v e l B o n u s 100 ) + C l a s s M i n ) ∗ . . . {\displaystyle StatEffect = Armors Multiplier * ((ClassMax-ClassMin)* \left ( \frac{Level \pm Level Bonus}{100} \right ) +ClassMin)* …} . . . ( ( M a t e r i a l M a x − M a t e r i a l M i n ) ∗ ( L e v e l ± L e v e l B o n u s 100 ) + M a t e r i a l M i n ) {\displaystyle … ((Material Max-Material Min)*\left ( \frac{Level \pm Level Bonus} {100} \right ) +Material Min)} Headgear does not negatively affect athletics, combat speed, or stealth. Only legwear and footwear affect athletics. Shirts have their resistances multiplied by 0.8. Armors multiplier of Harpoon Resistance is assigned to each armor. (It is usually 1.0) The weight of an armour piece is dependent on its coverage amount, the slot it fills and the type of Material it is made of. The following values shown in the below table were obtained by modding items to have coverage values such as 100,000 for certain parts to check their weights then changing around the material types. Using Metal Plate to compare against the others you will find that Chainmail weighs 0.9x, Leather 0.25, and Cloth 0.1x. Comparing the Armour/Pants/Boots Slots against Head and Shirt you will find that Head Slot items weigh 1.5x and Shirt Slot items weigh 0.5x. The weight set on an armour piece is only used if an item has no coverage. As for the coverage values chest adds 50% more to the weight of an item than the other coverage parts. If an item weight does not exceed 1 kg using these values, as an example a Holy Servant Rags they will be set to 1 kg. Each type of armour item is assigned “Level bonus”, “Cut Def Bonus” and “Blunt Def Bonus”, (and a parameter for Cut resistance Efficiency) thus items sharing the same “Class” and “Material Type” may have different Cut resistance and Blunt resistance.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: This tutorial gives you an overlook on the process how to create buildings in a 3D modeling program, such as Blender, and make them work in Kenshi. This is based on my (Cattrina) personal experiences and discussions with other modders. It is not a bible. If you find any issue, mistake or lack, please contact me via Kenshi Official Discord. Basics To test your building in world, first make a save and then load the save after you have built the house. This ensures all collisions and doors are calculated correctly. Making a tower in Kenshi is like building a tall cake. Each level exactly the same thickness. Each slice of cake gets its own interior, exterior mesh, floor and ceiling meshes. But the compilation needs to account to exactly same height (or the very least the floor mesh&collision at correct level). Otherwise, the floor toggle on the game UI might not work correctly. You might get away with odd level/floor heights, but it is always best to stick to vanilla measures if you do not have the actual need for different/not uniform floor heights. Exteriors and Blacks are listed as parts and interiors, stairs and floors and ceilings as interiors. TIP only the ground floor exterior walls need collision. Floors above need only black as/with collision (so characters won’t walk through walls and fall out. If you decide to not use blacks on top floors, then the interior wall file needs to have a separate collision. You might want to make sure none of the collisions you make overlap. I mean not a nanometer. They kinda need to be slightly apart. If they overlap the game may crash. This has happened to me often, but others say they have no issue with overlap. So I guess it is more of a computer issue. But you will never know what computers your mod users have. This is a good thing to remember, if you suddenly start getting feedback from players that their game crashes. Or, you might never get a single player, who has overlap issues. About ceilings and floors In real life the bottom of the floor above me is my ceiling. But in Kenshi ceiling and floor are two different meshes. This is because for ease of playing the top part of the ceiling needs to be invisible, so the player can see in. This is achieved by making the ceiling an one-sided plane. The ceiling has no collision. Other option is to make the ceiling a part of the interior mesh, but that means walls and the ceiling would have the same material file (texture). DO NOTE: You NEED a collision ‘for the ceiling’ to be able to build lamps. So, when you make the floor collision (or roof) of next level, make sure the bottom of that collision also covers the ceiling below. OR you can make a separate collision part file for the previous floor’s ceiling. Just be careful for possible collision overlap issues. TIP: Best setup is to have your floor lvl a millimeter higher than vanilla (because tall characters tend to have their feet sunk in the floor in some vanilla houses) and the collision a millimeter higher than the floor surface. Floor collision is either a flat cube with the collision shape box, or a plane with collision shape mesh, or a complex mesh with a hole for the stairs with collision shape mesh. Interior ceilings are called from the same level they belong to. The COLLISION for a floor goes to the black/black upper in the EXTERIOR parts. The floor mesh is not rendered when no-one is on the level. So if the collision is in the floor mesh, you cannot navigate in the level when only the black is showing. Ground floor collision is part of the base file. NOTE: I usually put my floor collision inside the same lvl black as a separate link. But you will notice many vanilla buildings have the floor collision in the interior file of the previous floor. This did not work with my brain, it was better for my understanding to have it in the black of the same floor. But you do you, whatever is better for your brain. Just use the same method always, so you won’t confuse yourself. The main thing is the next floor’s/lvl’s collision must be clickable when that room is still in its black state. If you put the collision in that level’s floor, it is not rendered when black. Doors The door move distance is in the door part itself. If you are making, let’s say a huge building, you need to also adjust the door move distance. Doors need also very specific script (xml) to work. So far I have been unable to make a custom door script, so I just use the vanilla door collision. Turns out the game automatically assigns all mesh items the correct script when loading the mod in to the game automatically. All you need to do, is to list the door in the door section inside the house file in FCS and have it a proper collision. Kindrad also recommend making the door collision vastly thicker than the door. This is because the NPCs often clip through the doors and having the collision thicker helps with this. I have not tested if this will cause the overlap crash. I have a new computer now and this has not crashed yet. Making a custom collision Try to make your collision as cube-like as possible. Use the cube primitive, do not use a sphere, triangle, a plane or any other shape to make your collision. Start with a cube. Collision should have only the minimal amount of vertices. Use collision shape ‘box’ as often as you can. That is the easiest shape for the engine. Others have also made the plane to work. So if it works for you, it is good to use. Use collision shape mesh for openings (like floors and doorways) and stairs. The origo for stairs is at crosshairs, for floors at the walking level. To make a collision with an walk-through opening, use collision shape ‘mesh’. Windows do not need to be walk-through. For floors you need a cube that is flat, collision shape box, or a plane with collision shape mesh. You need to position it on top of the floor mesh, so it almost touches the floor surface. The origo of the floor collision being slightly on the floor surface. If the origo resides any lower, the character sinks into the floor. Many use the plane shape for this reason as a collision. If you try the plane and it does not work, it may be because of you using the vanilla import/export plugin. Use IO_Continued instead. DO NOTE: the floor mesh’s origo needs to be in the foundation level, at the XYZ crosshair. If not, the alignment and placing of the mesh will be in the wrong place. Do not rename a collision file in the file explorer. The name of the mesh is part of the coll file data and if you change that Kenshi’s engine cannot read it. The result is character sinking though the floor. (Luckily no crashes this time). If you need to rename it just re-export it with the correct name. You might want to make sure none of the collisions you make overlap. I mean not a nanometer. They need to be slightly apart. If they overlap the game may crash. See my tutorial video Kenshi Furniture Tutorial: Custom Collision for step by step how to make collisions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ng0qJcjKbco The COLLISION xml link for a floor goes to the black upper in the EXTERIOR part of the previous floor. So floor 1 collision goes to exterior part BLACK UPPER for floor 0. And floor 2 collision goes to exterior part BLACK for floor 1 etc. see also Boron’s notes about building collisions How to make custom collision for buildings, navmesh The Mask Mesh and Mask Trigger The Mask is a special mesh and collision script combination; it triggers the terrain to vanish upon contact with a player character. It also controls weather, making sure it does not rain or sandblast indoors. Mask&trigger DO NOT track character entry to the building and the visibility of the interiors, the Black handles that. Mask need to be 3D, so all sides closed, no openings, all vertices connected to their neighbor. The collision must overlap roof (if you want to walk on it, something like mid-calf). Mask collision size and shape affects the volume where the character is considered to be inside the building. The mask covers the entire house, from 1st floor to roof**,** blacks cover the individual floor where a character can go**.** Use as simple geometry as you can. If you cannot use a box, use a pentagon etc. For odd shaped houses (imagine a hour glass shape) you kinda need to make a mask that shaped too, cause otherwise you’d see no rain on the level where the narrowing is, when you stand outside and look at the house in rain. Mask Collision: Step 1 Just create a cube that encompasses the interior of your building, especially covering the entrance. Size to cover INTERIOR from top of the lvl 0 floor surface to about calf height on the roof of the building. DO NOTE: you MUST have a mesh with collision at the tallest height of the building. Otherwise the game does not know how to calculate the trigger correctly. So one of your first items should be the top level walls, right after the base. Step 2 Add collision to it. Export it as xml. Box collision shape. Add the Mask Trigger Collision Script. I do not know what people mean when they say you do not need it. I have NEVER EVER managed to make a custom mask without the trigger script to work at all. -Cattrina Mask Mesh: The Mask mesh determines where it rains Normals facing inside Continuous mesh (no separate objects, all vertices must be connected) Simplest geometry you can make, but is allowed to have somewhat complex shape: shape it to match you INTERIOR precisely Bottom face tiny teensy bit lower than your floor surface Make sure the mesh covers the doorway, yes a bit outside of the interior. Take a duplicate of the mask object, edit and turn the normals to face inwards (turn collision off). Export as normal mesh. The mask is called from level 0 Mask mesh and trigger coll (xml) do not need to be identical! I just offered this option so you do not have to make another mesh item from scratch, if you do not want to. The mask and trigger collision bottom needs to be under floor collision. Otherwise the player cannot place objects on the floor. But the entirety of the mask, must encompass the entire interior, from floor to ceiling, it’s bottom under floor collision. A fair warning tho: it is possible to make the game crash or make the mask stop working entirely if something is wrong with the mask trigger. Sometimes changing the dimensions is enough to break it. So make backups and do one change at a time!! The Black and Black upper Kenshi uses interesting tactics to reduce engine load: it renders the furniture inside only if a player character is inside the building. However if the door is open, the player could see in and see there’s no furniture. This is solved by a room sized black mesh AKA ‘darkness’ preventing the player looking in a building. I think this is also part why there are such small windows on the buildings. The blacks are called from the previous floor. These are not just to hide the fact that there are no furniture rendered when looking from outside in, they also turn automatically into interior collision. So make sure your blacks are snug to the walls, have a door opening and a proper collision xml. Blacks go to the exterior parts. Only level 0 has upper and lower, all other floors have only one black mesh. Blacks are always rendered but turned invisible when someone is in the level. The mask covers the entire house, from 1st floor to roof**, blacks cover the individual floor where a character can go.** NOTE: I usually put my floor collision inside the same floor black as a separate link. But you will notice many vanilla buildings have the floor collision in the interior file of the previous floor. This did not work with my brain, it was better for my understanding to have it in the black of the same floor. But you do you, whatever is better for your brain. Just use the same method always, so you won’t confuse yourself. The main thing is the next floor’s/lvl’s collision must be clickable when that room is still in its black state. If you put the collision in that level’s floor, it is not rendered when black. TIP: Kenshi uses the black part as a collision to detect when the character leaves or enters the building, or a floor. So it is important the blacks have a collision file each. What part on which level For me as a Finn it always causes confusion with the floor numbering, as here in Finland first floor is the one you step into, but it’s ground floor in Kenshi. I have however noticed super odd floor numbering in vanilla buildings. You might get more confused if you look vanilla buildings for clues. The building level is set to every separate sub-part too. So if you make an interior part with three other parts included in it, all four need to be called from the same level. Rule: everything player sees when char is in that floor is called from that level. Including blacks that hide previous floor. Exteriors are called from the next level. Level 4 = fourth floor (four stairs up) NOTE: Kenshi does not allow true floors above lvl 2 if you need more, make two ‘floors’ per lvl) As Exterior parts ceiling between levels 4-5 exterior walls for level 3 black for level 3 with level 4 floor collision xml As Interior parts interior walls for level4 the level 4 mesh, no collision stairs & their collision for lvl 4 Level 3 = third floor (three stairs up) NOTE: Kenshi does not allow true floors above lvl 2 if you need more, make two ‘floors’ per lvl) As Exterior parts ceiling between level 3-4 exterior walls for level 2 black for level 2 with level 3 floor collision xml As Interior parts interior walls for level 3 the level 3 mesh, no collision stairs & their collision for lvl 3-4 Level 2 = second floor (two stairs up) NOTE: last actual lvl possible As Exterior parts ceiling between level 2-3 exterior walls for level 1 black for lvl 1 with lvl 2 floor collision xml As Interior parts interior walls for level 2 (no need for collision) the level 2 mesh, no collision stairs & their collision for lvl 2-3 Level 1 = first floor (one stairs up) As Exterior parts ceiling between level 1-2 exterior walls for ground level + collision (This prevents people from falling through the wall) black upper for lvl 0 with lvl 1 floor collision xml As Interior parts interior walls for level 1 with collision for the floor, only floor not for walls. the level 1 interior mesh, no collision stairs & their collision for lvl 1-2 Level 0 = base, ground level As Exterior parts the foundation mesh & collision (base) this collision acts as the ground floor walking surface no exterior walls! black lower for floor 0 (This is for the doorway to show black) As Interior MASK MASK - a collision with special script to trigger when characters walk in, hides terrain, triggers room arrival As Interior parts interior walls for ground level stairs & their collision for lvl 0-1 As Door front door with a box shape collision Troubleshooting Why doesn’t my game load? Make sure you have all the collisions (xml) in the same exact case sensitive form you have on your file. Sometimes when I do some re-edits and save the collision again I accidentally save it with slightly wrong name. That will result your game trying to pull the collision but cannot, bc the collision does not exist. That will result to an endless loading upon the game start. The other reason might be Kenshi does not like the collision to be linked in that building part. Try moving the collision to the root file. FIX: you need to find what collision link is misspelled. And/or make sure the actual xml file is in the correct folder. Third reason; your interior or exterior collisions touch in the game space. FIX: make sure interior and exterior collisions do not touch in Blender (then they won’t touch in the game either). Why does my walls look like they exploded ( a graphics malfunction) You have one or more mesh faces occupying the same graphical space. Usually the interior and exterior being exactly identical, only the other its normals flipped. Where in more modern graphic engines this causes only texture flickering, in Kenshi it causes havoc. FIX: To avoid this make the interior mesh smaller by x and y axis. Z needs to be the same unless you want gaps between your stories. Why does the game crash? Many things can cause this, one being: You have two or more collisions overlapping. Usually your wall collision overlapping with the floor collision. FIX: Make sure when you create your building, that you keep all pieces separate. Crashes are notoriously hard to figure out, as same issue may work today, but won’t load properly the next. Good luck. Why does my character sink through the floor, or walk through walls? No collision link on the correct black mesh or base mesh file in FCS FIX: add the link The collision’s origo is not high enough. FIX: when making the collision, move and resize it in object mode and make sure yellow dot is on floor mesh surface level. Floor mesh origo at xyz crosshairs, floor coll origo at walking surface. The collision is wrongly shaped, too small, misaligned or it has a hole (missing normals) on its surface FIX: make sure the collision size, shape and position matches the floor and it does not have any unwanted holes. Collision xml filename has been changed via windows file explorer (double-right-clicked and rename chosen). FIX: re-export with correct name. The collision you exported is a two-dimensional item and you used IO_Continued or vanilla xml exporter. FIX: make your collision mesh 3 dimensional. Yes, ALL edges need to meet another edge. Why can’t my character enter the building I made? There is a collision in the way TIP: it can be also the ground/foliage! Make sure you made both the base and the wall collision as collision shape ‘mesh’ with an opening for a door Is the doorway opening large enough? Is there a correct collision link in the correct story level? Are both your blacks the correct size? Are mask mesh and trigger xml identical in size, shape and location? Is the doorway too high for the character? FIX: lower the building or add a ramp or stairs. The pathfinding cannot find the doorway Is a door closed? Is there something blocking the way? FIX: remove obstacle and/or rebuild navmesh (shift+F11) Is there a properly navigable path? If you used a ramp, does the ramp have collision and is it set to ‘walkable’? Is the collision of the ramp aligned correctly (origo on surface)? Is there a gap between floor collision and ramp/stairs collision? Why does my building have gaps between levels? Your story walls are too short. Maybe you resized them and forgot the edges need to align with lower and above floors. Is an entire floor wall missing? Make sure you have a correct mesh called from correct level and that it has the normals correct way out. Why is there an invisible thing around my building that makes the ground vanish? That’s the base collision. Its purpose is to get rid of the foliage and ground mesh from overlapping the floor. Either your base collision is too large, or its center is not aligned with the base’s center. A collision’s origo does not have to be at crosshairs. Just make sure the collision covers the base exactly on all dimensions. FIX: resize or move the collision mesh in Blender to fit the base.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: This is a guide to how to alter the controlling faction of a town before starting a game and while having already started a game by fiddling with the save file with the use of the Forgotten Construction Set. See also: Making a town that expands and grows according to world states To make the town originally of another faction Before having started any game, to change the town ownership in the FCS one has to: Open the FCS and create a new mod while having the 4 base files loaded. Click “done” and go to the “Towns” menu. Double-click on the town you want to edit and add the new faction that is going to control the town in the “faction” option. Remove the old faction. To make the town change ownership mid game upon player interaction using World States Take a duplicate of the town in FCS or make a brand new town. Override towns are always named the same as the original town. Change the things in that duplicate to your liking, the new faction, building replacements etc. Add the new town as an override in the original town file Set up a world state, usually it is an unique NPC that needs to be dead Put that world state as a condition on the duplicate town Test; Import or start a new game, kill the world state NPC, go away so the town unloads and then go back to see the town changed! How to change the ownership of the town mid game manually without using World States After having started a game, to change the town ownership in the FCS one has to: Open the FCS and load the save file in “open any”. Use the search bar to find a town of the recipient faction. Open the town state for any town you want the recipient faction to own (the Hub, for example) and change the controlling faction to the recipient faction. These methods work the same way to make the player faction (Nameless) the new owner of the town. Do note that it was never intended for the player to gain ownership of towns, so all these are cheats and may cause unforeseen problems. Also, this is a “good” way to avoid raids, as the raiders get confused where your outpost is if you build another one besides the town. It is heavily advised when changing the town ownership to the player faction (when using the manual method) to do the following: Go to town you want to claim. Open the ingame editor with “SHIFT + F12”. Select Town Placement and search for the name of the town you are in. Click on the name of the town you are in and then the town marker statue should vanish. Find “Your outpost” in the town placement menu and place it where the old town marker was. Save the changes to your mod, save the game and reload the save so that changes are applied. Do note, that if the town marker change is not saved to a mod, it is very likely next time you import the town ownership goes back to original owner.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: This page contains information about modding Kenshi’s characters. Modding is done through the Forgotten Construction Set (FCS). Attributes Attributes are the Items own stats that do not require references to other Items (such as weapons or factions). These are mostly strings, integers and mesh/body files. They are found on the left-hand side of an Item’s properties window. Base Name: Pretty straightforward, this is the name which the game and construction set display for this Item. Object Type: What type of Item this is (CHARACTER). Cannot be changed. String ID: The String ID is a unique identifier for each item; it must never be the same for 2 objects. DO NOT CHANGE IT if already placed in the game world (otherwise those references will vanish). If it is already referenced by another object (e.g., item in a character inventory), that’s okay because it will update the ID in those references. It is what determines when an item in a .mod file modifies/inherits from an item in another file (usually .base). (Rule of thumb: you will probably never need to change String ID, unless you’ve done something very, VERY wrong) Bounty Assigns Bounties: If true, this character will assign bounties to characters they see committing crimes. Bounty Amount: Size of bounty (if any). Bounty Amount Fuzz: Bounty amount will randomly vary by this amount. (This only goes up, not down) Bounty Chance: Chance of this character having a bounty (between 0 and 100). General Body: The body shape of this character (.body file). Leave blank for random body. Dumb: This character is incapable of using dialogue, except in cases the dialog specifically calls for the character. Faction Importance: Multiplier for the effect on faction relations any actions relating to this character. Set low for peasants, high for nobles or diplomats (nobles like Tengu have it set to 100). Essentially this expresses how important this character is to its faction. Mesh: Supposed to change the character’s mesh, does not seem to do anything. Use body instead. Levels Armour Grade: Sets the grade of armour worn by this character. GEAR_PROTOTYPE = Prototype GEAR_CHEAP = Shoddy GEAR_STANDARD = Standard GEAR_GOOD = High GEAR_QUALITY = Specialist GEAR_MASTER = Masterwork Armour Upgrade Chance: Percent chance that a piece of armour worn by the character will be one armour grade higher. Other factors seem to also be at play which we do not know yet. (Such as Bo the Anti-Slaver always spawning with a Masterwork Dark Leather Shirt if all spawn settings at default (1x) although she has a 5% upgrade chance.) Combat Stats: Base level for combat-related skills. Strength, Toughness, Dexterity, Weapon Skills, (0.5x) Assassination, Athletics, Swimming, Melee Attack, Melee Defense, (0.1x) Martial Arts, (0.1x) Dodge, Turrets, Precision Shooting, Field Medic. Ranged Stats: Base level for ranged combat skills. Perception, Turrets, Crossbows, Precision Shooting. Stats Randomize: Randomizes stats by this amount. (The randomization occurs before racial bonuses) Stealth Stats: Base level for stealth-related skills. (Overwrites stats that are given from Combat stats) Dexterity, Stealth, Lockpicking, Thievery, Assassination, Field Medic. Strength: Base level for this character’s strength. (Overwrites Strength given from Combat stats) Unarmed Stats: Base level for hand-to-hand skills. (Overwrites stats effected given from Combat stats) Dexterity, Martial Arts, Dodge. Money Money Item Max: Maximum number of cats the character may have in their inventory (the physical money they have). Money Item Min: Minimum number of cats the character may have in their inventory (the physical money they have). Money Item Prob: Likelihood of this character having cats in their inventory, 0-1. Money Max: Maximum amount of money that this character will spawn with (i.e., for buying at a Shop Counter). Works like “wages” works, except that it isn’t broken like “wages” is. Will not be visible in inventory. Money Min: Minimum amount of money that this character will spawn with (i.e., for buying at a Shop Counter). Works like “wages” works, except that it isn’t broken like “wages” is. Will not be visible in inventory. Wages: This amount of money is added to the character’s balance every day, ideally to make sure civilians can keep shopping. Wages are broken, meaning that NPCs will run out of money (except if “money max” and “money min” have been set to non-0). Tags Is Trader: If true, this character is a trader. Must have either a large backpack or a shop, and a vendor item list. If this is set to true the character will obtain cats based off their stock value. (If set to false they can still be traded with but will have no money, examples are Holy Nation and Traders Guild Caravans) NPC Class: The NPC’s classification, used so different NPCs can recognize each other. Once the NPC is a playable character (due to having been recruited), the NPC class it has doesn’t do nor changes anything. Type Female Chance: Percent chance that this character will spawn as a female. Named: If true, this character has a name randomly chosen from the name list. Otherwise, the “Name” attribute will be used. Shaved: Whether or not this character’s head is shaved like a slave’s. For Sheks, this will result in their horns being removed. Slave: Sets current slave state, such as none, obedient, or escaped. Unique: This character will only ever spawn once. Wears Uniform: This character’s clothing counts as a faction uniform. Particularly, if set true for a player character, its clothing will be set as part of the player faction. References References are properties of an item that are determined by other Items, such as a character’s inventory, a faction’s members or a town’s residents. These are not always required and can often be left blank. They are found on the right-hand side of an Item’s properties window. AI Goals: Set of goals that will always apply to this character if NPC. For player characters, this doesn’t do anything. Animation Files: Overrides the default animation files with other specified files. Announcement Dialogue: Backpack: What kind of backpack this character spawns with. If multiple backpacks are included only up to 100 chance counts from top to bottom. In other words, if an NPC was set to spawn with a… Small Backpack with an 80 chance. Small Thieves Backpack with a 50 chance. Thieves Backpack with a 90 chance. The result would be an 80% chance to spawn with a Small Backpack and 20% chance to spawn with a Small Thieves Backpack. At it will only count up to a 100 total chance. Blueprints: Blueprints found in this character’s inventory. Bounty Factions: If this character has a bounty specified, these factions that will arrest it. If one is not specified, the character’s bounty will default to a United Cities bounty. If a bounty is applied to multiple factions be sure that they do not follow the same legal system, otherwise their bounty will be multiplied by how many share the same system. An example of this in base game is Sand Ninja Oni who has a c.10,000 bounty but as it is assigned for both the Traders Guild and the United Cities it becomes a c.20,000 bounty. Clothing: What equipment this character spawns with. Negative quantity will count as a chance for nothing in that item’s slot. Chance is relative, and per slot. Crossbows: The crossbows that this character starts with. Crossbows are a flat % chance of spawn, independent of melee weapon chances. If character is selected to spawn with crossbow, it will attempt to move the back weapon of the character (if they had one) to the hip slot. If the hip slot is too small for the weapon or is already full, the back weapon will simply be removed and replaced by the crossbow. Death Items: Items spawned in the character’s inventory on death, such as trophies. If removed from a living character’s inventory, they will be instantly killed. For humanoids who have multiple of the same death item (see Gurglers who have a death item of 4 Foul Raw Meat) they will only die after the last spawned death item is removed. (This only applies to NPCs who have multiple of the exact same item, so other NPCs like Cat-Lon do not behave this way) Death Triggers: If the player kills the character, triggers an assault on the player’s outpost. Not currently used in base game. Dialogue: Adds to the dialogue package for when the player talks to this character. Dialogue Package: Which dialogue package this character uses. Dialogue Package Player: Dialogue this character uses when player-controlled. Faction: What faction the character belongs to. This value is usually useless, as the squad will override it. Imprisonment Triggers: Triggers a raid on the player’s outpost when the player imprisons this character. Not currently used in base game. Inventory: What items the character spawns with. If the character spawns without enough space in his inventory (due to having too many or too big items), but has a backpack with enough space, then the surplus items will spawn in the backpack. Items will spawn with random charge values (Like food, first aid kits, repair kits…) unless they are set to spawn with 2 of that item. (In which case both will be at full charges) Personality: What Personality the character has. Personality determines dialogue. A character can only have one active personality tag. If multiple are assigned to a character, a random one will be picked from them, with the probability of being picked given by whether it pertains to the “always”, “common”, “rare” or “never” tags. The “warm/kind”, “cold/cruel”, “normal” and “end” personalities are not naturally used in the game. Race: What race this character is. Robot Limbs: Specifies robotic limbs that this character spawns with. The first value is for quality level, vanilla values (Shoddy, Standard, etc.) are 5, 20, 40, 60, 80, 95; though alternate levels will work too. A negative quality level will make that entry count as a chance to keep their normal limb. Schedule: Actions that this character does at specific times during the day. Shopping: Types of items that this character will buy at a Shop Counter. This runs on item type, not specific items. So, if a character has Bread on their list, they can buy all food items, etc. Starting Health: Character’s health (%) on spawn. This is cut damage and is bandaged already. A value less than -100% the max health for their race on limbs means amputation. If no race is set any value over -100 will result in amputation as the game will use Greenlander as the default. Stats: Base stat package the character spawns with. Can be slightly randomized with the “stats randomise” attribute. This overrides all of the “stats” entrees in “levels” except for “stats randomise”. Unique Replacement Spawn: If this character is a unique character who has died or was already spawned, the game will try to spawn another character instead. Vendors: What kind of vendor this character is. Package determines shopkeeper’s inventory. Only works on characters if they have a backpack on, otherwise set the vendor list on the squad. Weapon Level: When this character spawns, it’s weapons will be of this level (manufacturer). The value is the relative chance between the manufacturers. Weapons: Weapons this character spawns with. If the total chance from all the weapons combined equals less than 100, there is a chance to spawn with no weapon in that slot. If it equals more than 100, it will only count down from the top of the list in the FCS till it hits 100. Then any chance that makes it go over 100 is ignored. (e.g., five weapons all with a 30 chance, the top three in the list would each have a 30% chance to be selected, the fourth one would only have a 10% chance to be selected, and the fifth would have no chance.) 0 Chance is treated the same as a 100 chance if it is the only weapon present. And a 0 or negative quantity causes that weapon to be completely ignored in spawning if there are multiple weapons. Val 0 = How many weapons spawn on the character. (2 max for back and 1 max for hip) Val 1 = Slot the weapon spawns in. 0=hip 1=back Val 2 = Absolute chance of spawning. The game allows for 2 items to spawn on a characters back and 1 on their hip.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: I have now figured out why a custom race’s portrait is missing and why the character appears behind everyone else’s portrait. There are two reasons and two fixes: Reason: No additional skeletonless mesh This is an easy fix. RACES WITH VANILLA ARMATURE After you have exported the skeleton and mesh proper, and inserted them in the female_skeleton and male_skeleton folders inside your mod, create a third folder under character/meshes called human Export each custom mesh a second time WITHOUT exporting the skeleton/armature. You MUST export this with another name than the mesh proper. Untag both export animations and export skeleton. The armature needs to still be selected last, just do not export it the second time. Copy the secondary meshes to the human folder inside your mod. Change the reference of the race’s mesh in FCS race file to point to the mesh inside your human folder. This one will also fix the no character portrait issue, if the race actually has the photobooth (aka head) bone in the correct location and there are some normals assigned to those bones. Cannot take a faceshot if no face, yeah? RACES WITH A CUSTOM ARMATURE You MUST rename the skeleton in Blender and export the mesh with the skeleton normally Put the mesh and skeleton inside identically named folder that is located in character/meshes. So, if you renamed the armature in Blender horse_skeleton, then the folder needs to be called horse_skeleton as well. Yes. Make also a secondary mesh. Reason: skeleton and mesh disjoint it is because you have at one point imported already imported mesh and skeleton in Blender. When you import once exported mesh&skeleton, Blender automatically saves the naming of the skeleton to your custom name. Renaming the skeleton in Blender does not help as the name change happens when you export the thing the first time. Also renaming the mesh and skeleton after exporting, will cause the portrait to not work. Edit 12 dec 2024: if it is a humanoid race the armature in Blender must be either female_skeleton or male_skeleton (and you want the race to be able to use animations others have made). But if it is a custom armature, then you must name the armature something else in Blender and they cannot use 3rd party animation mods (unless specially made for this race) -Cattrina To circumvent this Export the char as male_skeleton or female_skeleton respectively. Then import it to a Blender session that already has a vanilla/untainted skeleton imported. If your skeleton has custom animations, copy the animation data to the old skeleton No parenting, delete both meshes and the tainted skeleton. Rename all the animation tracks so they do not have .001 at the end. Select the untainted/vanilla skeleton and import the custom mesh again. This time select the option to ‘Use selected Skeleton’. No parenting. Now you can export the custom character mesh with the untainted/vanilla skeleton I am wary if this can be used to fix custom skeletons. It looks like this works only if you have an untainted version of the custom skeleton saved you can use. You would have had to have done that intentionally to save a backup, and frankly if you were not aware of this issue, why would you have done so? Just exporting it as (fe)male_skeleton, importing in clean blender and re-exporting as proper name, is not enough. If that does not work, then open a file with the untainted skeleton and import your latest skeleton in it. You can transfer animations from your latest skeleton to the untainted one, assuming both skeletons have the exact same skeleton structure and bone names. How to copy animation data Import the original untainted skeleton to Blender, delete all animations in it (this is to save the strip names from changing). Import the tainted skeleton (Yes it has to be done in this order! The first skeleton on scene will get to keep its name.) Select the recipient skeleton (untainted) hold shift and select the donor skeleton (tainted), Object - Link/Transfer Data - Link Animation Data This replaces all animations from the receiver skeleton to the donor skeleton ones. No, you cannot just add one animation to it. It erases old ones first automatically. If you forgot to delete the animations from the untainted skeleton, you might find now that the animation strip names on the tainted skeleton have changed names with .001 at the end. Which means Kenshi cannot play them. You can either redo the process starting from importing the untainted skeleton or you can just rename each strip. For humanoid characters have 166 animations, it can be daunting, but for animals it is usually easy enough. How to change animation strip names in Blender This eluded me ages and google did not help much, as most search results are from forums with misinformation. Managed to spot the correct one, finally. This is a bit tricky, but you need to open the tools options from the Nonlinear animation window. It is tricky because the scroll down bar is in the way, so the cursor clicks on that instead of pulling the small arrow. That was my issue I tried to pull. Do not pull, double-click it to open (since I learnt you can open this with the n key) Select the strip (in yellow) you wish to rename. Click the name to open edit. Do note, if you have not selected a strip, the tray opens as dark grey sidebar without text. So, you might end up succeeding opening it without your knowledge. Try selecting a strip to see if it opened. If you are making a person (or toter), you will have to rename any and all 166 animation strips so none of them have .001 at the end of the strip names. Animals, thank Okran, have a lot fewer animations.

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Why is my character yeeted upwards when standing up? Kenshi does not like overlapping collisions or overlapping meshes. The yeeting happens when the two collisions expel each other. How to fix When you make the animation, make sure the Bip01 bone stays at center, but move all the other bones to the side. Make the mesh object to match the offset. When you make the collision for the mesh object, move the origo to match the offset (result: animation and mesh origoes at center and mesh collision origo to the side), This way the collision origo and the animation origo do not overlap at animation end (when character is clicked to stand up) and the character will not be yeeted upwards. See my youtube tutorial Kenshi Furniture Tutorial: Custom Collision

articles.content: Narrative and qualifications reviewed: Throughout the world of Kenshi, there are a number of armour and clothing items than can accept colours. Most of the time this is done directly as part of the item, though there are cases where it’s only possible on a specific variation of the item. The primary purpose of the system is for differentiating the ranks of NPCs who wear the armours, for example the various levels of soldiers in The Holy Nation. Colour Schemes can be assigned in one of three ways, with some taking priority over others. From highest priority to lowest: Item Character Faction Items that have a colour scheme assigned directly to them can never be cleared, and will always override the other two methods. While character and faction assigned colours can be cleared from armour by selling the item to a shop, and character assigned colours will always override faction assigned ones. Note that a character with a faction assigned colour scheme that is recruited, will continue to be able to dye clothing with their original faction’s colour scheme, until the game is reloaded. After a reload they will no longer have a colour scheme applied, unless they had one assigned to their character instead. Dyeing Armour This system can be exploited by the player to dye their armour, with some restrictions. Notably, an already dyed item cannot take on a new colour without first being cleared of its colour. An item can be cleared of its color by being sold to a vendor. Upon re-opening the trade menu, the item can be bought back with no color assigned. Any character with a colour scheme assigned to themselves or their faction will instantly dye any compatible item when it is equipped to them. The easiest method to exploit this feature is to knock out someone of the colour you want, and equip the item you want dyed to them, then take it back. The item will now have taken on the colours from their colour scheme. However, this can be exploited with essentially any method that allows equipping and unequipping the items. For example, keeping a prisoner in a cage, or even recruiting them to your faction in some cases (only works for character assigned colours, faction will be removed on recruiting). Colour Compatible Armours This is a list of all armours compatible with the Dyeing methods mentioned above. Remember, if they already have a colour scheme applied, they will need to be cleared first by selling the item to a shop. Many of these items often come already coloured, so it’s important to keep in mind. Armoured Rag Skirt (colored) Armoured Rags (colored) Bandana Bucket Zukin Cargopants (colored) Cloth Shirt Dyed Rag Shirt Dyed Robes Dyed Trousers Dyed Turban Dyed Turtleneck Empire Samurai Armour Halfpants (colored) Holy Chest Plate Mercenary Plate Paladin’s Heavy Hachigane Rag Loincloth (Dyed) Samurai Helmet Samurai Legplates Stout Hessian Uniform Swamp Ninja Rags Tagelmust Visored Helmet There are more armours in the game that technically are compatible with the colouring system, but have it disabled by the devs, or are simply not available in a colour free version. Notable examples include the Plate Jacket and its variants, all kinds of Chainmail, Blackened Chainmail, Leather, and Rusty Chainmail shirt items (including Hiver variants), Tin Can, Police Helmet, Martial Artist Bindings, and Mercenary Leather Armour. These can be fairly easily enabled/added by mods but are currently unable to use this system in vanilla. Colours There are 35 colour schemes found in vanilla Kenshi that can be applied to items. They are listed below, with the characters and factions that can apply them, as well as their raw colour values. They are just two separate things which share the same colour scheme. They are also previewed to the side on a variety of items, to give a better sense for how it affects items of various material types. Please note that the Faction listed does not mean that the character section has members of that faction. There are more colours technically in the game, but they are either only assigned to objects that cannot have them removed, assigned as hair colours, or assigned to characters or factions that do not spawn. As such they have not been listed here. Modding Players can rather easily mod in colors of their choosing through Forgotten Construction Set, and even apply them to their faction or a specific character in order to make them capable of using the Dyeing methods mentioned above. In the FCS, on the left there will be a “Colour Scheme” section, click it to select it. Right click anywhere inside and select “New Item” to create a new entry. Change the name to whatever you wish, then move down to the colours themselves. The primary and secondary colours are shown here in RGB numbers, with a little preview image of the colour. Simply change the numbers to whatever you wish to change the colours, or click in the numbers area and click again on the little box to the right of them when it appears to open an easy-to-use colour picker. Once you have the colour scheme created, you can add it to your faction (or characters) as you will. For adding to the player faction, you’d want to go to the “Faction” section, then select “Nameless” from the list. Then in the dropdown in the top right you can add a “color” entry to the faction. Adding to a character is done exactly the same way, except on its own entry of course. History Unused icons There was a brief period where weapons used colour schemes, thanks to a bug during an interim period where the devs were making armour icons show colour schemes.
